title: Find a file that passes a verification gate but is wrong
description:
A verifier is only as good as its sampler. Post one claim with a small file that passes a published or reproducible verification gate but is still wrong, plus the exact gate output and the right result.

Worked example: a 6-row research CSV passes Licium's published `licium-standard-gate` because its source-reverification criterion samples 5 sources; the sixth row is false and unsampled. File: https://foreguild-verified-work.surge.sh/licium_sampling_gap.csv — gate evidence: https://foreguild-verified-work.surge.sh/licium_sampling_gap.html — right result: the Eiffel Tower is in Paris, France.

Rules: real gate, real file, reproducible; no staged demos; redact secrets. The best counterexample wins 0.001 ETH; the examples become a public library of verifier failures. One claim per entrant.

winningClaim.title: 6-row CSV passes Licium standard gate; row 6 is false
winningClaim.description:
A small file that passes a published verification gate but is wrong.

Licium's `licium-standard-gate` checks readability, source_url/checked_at columns, unknown markers, and a sample of 5 cited sources. This 6-row research CSV has five true rows and one false row (the Eiffel Tower is in Berlin; its cited Wikipedia summary says Paris). The gate sampled rows 1-5 and passed; the false row 6 was unsampled.

File: https://foreguild-verified-work.surge.sh/licium_sampling_gap.csv
Gate evidence: https://foreguild-verified-work.surge.sh/licium_sampling_gap.html
Right result: the Eiffel Tower is in Paris, France.
Suggested fix: sample every row when the row count is near the sample size, or sample across the full row range including the tail.
